disease_label_per_paper: Henoch-Schonlein purpura with intussusception and hematochezia in an adult
presentation_summary: A 19-year-old man had mild vomiting and a rash on the joints and soft tissue of the extremities ten days before admission.
He then developed diarrhea followed by right lower intermittent cramping abdominal pain over four hours.
Laboratory studies showed WBC 13.1 x10^9/L, neutrophils 81%, and hemoglobin 136 g/L.
Occult stool testing and urinalysis were positive; stool microscopy showed a large number of red blood cells.
CT showed swollen jejunal loops with suspicious target/doughnut sign.
He was diagnosed with Henoch-Schonlein purpura with intussusception based on typical clinical symptoms and imaging.
Abdominal pain deteriorated and he developed strong abdominal muscle tension consistent with peritonitis.

Emergency laparotomy found the ileocecal junction intussuscepted 20 cm into the ascending colon without perforation or necrosis; a large subserosal hematoma 15 cm from the ileocecal junction was considered the lead cause.
Manual release of the ileocecal intussusception and ileocecal junction repair were performed.
Postoperatively he resumed liquid diet day 1, semi-liquid day 3, and normal food intake by day 7 without abnormal exhaust or defecation.

clinical_course.event: Mild vomiting and extremity rash began.
Diarrhea followed by right lower cramping abdominal pain; CT suggested intussusception.
Pain worsened with abdominal muscle tension; emergency laparotomy reduced ileocecal intussusception.
Normal food intake resumed without abnormal exhaust or defecation.

outcome.source_text_value: On the seventh day after surgery, the patient had normal food intake, and no abnormalities in exhaust and defecation were reported in the visible case text.

quality_warnings: The paper does not report skin or renal biopsy for this case; it diagnoses HSP/IgA vasculitis from typical symptoms and imaging.
